macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. futures rise ahead of September jobs report
items.summary: S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq futures moved higher as investors awaited the September employment report for clues about the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision. Consensus called for roughly 84,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate.

items.title: Global bond sell-off keeps pressure on markets
items.summary: Asian shares were mixed after a sharp rise in government-bond yields. Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.9%, while South Korea’s Kospi, Australia’s ASX 200 and Taiwan’s Taiex gained; the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained near multiyear highs.

items.title: Wall Street ends slightly higher as Treasury yields retreat
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.2%, the Dow gained less than 0.1% and the Nasdaq added less than 0.1% in a choppy session. A rebound in Treasuries helped offset concerns about elevated energy costs and inflation.

items.title: Fed officials signal patience on further rate increases
items.summary: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said policymakers may need more time to assess whether additional interest-rate increases are necessary. Markets continued to focus on incoming labor and inflation data ahead of the Fed’s next decision.

items.title: Nike warns of revenue decline as turnaround continues
items.summary: Nike shares fell after the company reported weaker-than-expected results and forecast declining fiscal 2027 revenue. Management cited weakness in China, sportswear and the Jordan brand while continuing an operational overhaul.

items.title: Micron delivers upbeat outlook on AI demand
items.summary: Micron posted quarterly results above expectations and issued a strong current-quarter outlook, supported by demand tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company warned that rising compensation costs would pressure margins.

items.title: Accenture results benefit from AI demand
items.summary: Accenture reported fourth-quarter profit of $1.99 billion, or $3.29 per share, compared with $1.41 billion, or $2.25 per share, a year earlier. The company also booked stronger-than-expected new business.

items.title: Amazon agrees to major nuclear-power purchase from Constellation
items.summary: Amazon agreed to purchase 690 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy, supporting expansion at the nuclear operator’s Maryland facilities and helping meet electricity demand associated with data centers.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: SEC proposes easing crypto custody rules for investment advisers
items.summary: The SEC proposed allowing investment advisers to hold clients’ crypto assets when no eligible custodian is available, while also permitting state trust companies to act as crypto custodians. New York and Wyoming separately agreed to coordinate oversight of crypto firms.[3]

items.title: EU regulators scrutinize Binance’s MiCA exemption
items.summary: ESMA and regulators in France, Germany and Greece are reportedly examining Binance’s reliance on MiCA’s reverse-solicitation exemption to continue serving some European customers without direct authorization.[3]

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $85,000 as liquidations accelerate
items.summary: Bitcoin reached approximately $85,111, gaining about 5.7% in the reported period, while roughly $648 million in short positions were liquidated. Separate market data placed BTC above $86,000 later in the session.[6][5]

items.title: Ether gains more than 3% in 24 hours
items.summary: Ether rose to about $2,754 and was reported up 3.38% over 24 hours, with short liquidations across three exchanges totaling approximately $17.1 million during one hour.[5]

items.title: CFTC provides relief for crypto software developers
items.summary: The CFTC issued a no-action position shielding certain crypto software developers from introducing-broker registration, expanding earlier relief granted to wallet provider Phantom.[6]

items.title: ZetaChain governance approves move to Solana
items.summary: A governance vote reportedly passed with 99.4% support to shut down ZetaChain’s Cosmos-based layer-1 and migrate ZETA to Solana as an SPL token at a 1:1 ratio.[6]

items.title: Singapore crypto payments firm dtcpay raises $25 million
items.summary: dtcpay completed a $25 million Series A round led with strategic investment from Japan’s SBI Group, targeting merchant-network expansion and new consumer features.[6]

items.title: NEAR Intents attacker identified after $3.8 million drain
items.summary: NEAR Intents’ general manager said the attacker behind a preliminary $3.8 million theft had been identified and published three addresses for returning the funds.[2]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon to selected cybersecurity testers
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model aimed at coding, enterprise workflows, and cybersecurity. Initial access is limited to trusted testers through its Fairwind program, with Google highlighting long-context and software-engineering performance.[1][10]

items.title: AMD agrees to acquire World Labs for about $8.2 billion
items.summary: AMD announced a deal to acquire AI company World Labs, co-founded by Fei-Fei Li, in a transaction valued at approximately $8.2 billion. Li is expected to become AMD’s executive vice president and chief scientist, subject to regulatory approval.[3]

items.title: SoftBank completes $10 billion OpenAI investment
items.summary: SoftBank reportedly completed a $10 billion investment in OpenAI, underscoring the continuing flow of capital into frontier-model development and AI infrastructure.[1]

items.title: Broadcom to provide Anthropic up to $42 billion for TPU infrastructure
items.summary: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic as much as $42 billion to support infrastructure expansion, including a multiyear lease involving large-scale Google TPU capacity.[1]

items.title: OpenAI launches Dots, an agent-oriented assistant feature
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Dots, a capability designed to provide more persistent, agent-like assistance across tasks and workflows, intensifying competition in consumer AI assistants.[6]

items.title: Nvidia expands share-repurchase authorization by $150 billion
items.summary: Nvidia’s board approved a $150 billion increase to its share-buyback authorization, leaving $235 billion available through fiscal 2028 as demand for AI accelerators continues to drive strong cash generation.[6]

items.title: Mistral AI opens Munich hub for physics and industrial AI
items.summary: Mistral AI announced a Munich research and engineering hub focused on Physics AI and Industrial AI, with planned work involving BMW and Siemens Energy and an ambition to build one gigawatt of European compute capacity by 2030.[3]

items.title: Modal Labs reportedly seeks $750 million funding round
items.summary: AI inference infrastructure company Modal Labs is reportedly nearing a $750 million financing round led by Accel, potentially valuing the company at $15.75 billion.[3]

items.title: Runway unveils Praxis-1 robot-control model
items.summary: Runway introduced Praxis-1, a world model applying video pretraining to robot control. The company said three partners are testing it on different hardware and that model weights are expected to be released in the coming months.[2]

items.title: Bank of America plans to double AI spending next year
items.summary: Bank of America plans to increase annual AI spending to about $800 million, building on roughly 140 AI and machine-learning projects and an estimated $800 million in benefits identified by the bank.[2]
